brief: ING expects a 25bp Fed hike Wednesday, not the 50bp the note argues could better fit Chair Warsh's own critique of Fed guidance shaping the market pricing that the Fed then simply delivers. The market prices over 90% probability of a hike, moving the fed funds range to 3.75-4%. A 50bp move would let the Fed take control and could calm the long end by showing active protection, but could instead destabilize it by validating the 100bp rise in the 10-year yield over the past six months and triggering a follow-through sell-off. No change is called unlikely since it could hurt the long end. Separately, ING sees term premium continuing to build and curves bear steepening: the 30-year Japanese government bond yield is rising again, euro swap liquidity at long tenors is thin, and US deficit concerns persist, keeping long-end yields sticky even if oil eases. ING expects that upward pressure to sustain for now but turns more pessimistic on the US economic outlook for 2027.
